q: 设计原则在 LLD 面试中的主要作用是什么？
q_en: What is the main role of design principles in an LLD interview?
options: 帮助你做类和抽象的取舍，并说清楚理由
要求你逐字背出每个原则的缩写
替代面试里的需求澄清环节
保证任何设计都必须足够复杂
options_en: They help you make and explain tradeoffs about classes and abstractions.
They require you to recite every acronym word for word.
They replace the requirements-clarification step.
They guarantee every design must be sufficiently complex.
why: 面试官更在意你是否用原则做出并解释好设计，而不是你能不能像背单词一样报出 SOLID。
why_en: Interviewers care whether you use design principles to make and explain good tradeoffs, not whether you can recite SOLID from memory.

termDefinitions.fullName: Single Responsibility, Open/Closed, Liskov Substitution, Interface Segregation, Dependency Inversion
termDefinitions.meaning: SOLID：SRP、OCP、LSP、ISP、DIP 五项面向对象设计原则的合称。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SOLID is the acronym for five object-oriented design principles: Single Responsibility, Open/Closed, Liskov Substitution, Interface Segregation, and Dependency Inversion.

q: 如果只能优先记住三个通用软件设计原则，应该选哪三个？（多选）
q_en: If you could only prioritize three general software design principles, which three should they be? (multi-select)
options: KISS
DRY
YAGNI
CAP 定理
options_en: KISS
DRY
YAGNI
the CAP theorem
why: KISS、DRY、YAGNI 覆盖复杂度、重复和过早设计三类常见问题；CAP 定理是分布式一致性话题，不是这篇 LLD 原则的重点。
why_en: KISS, DRY, and YAGNI matter most because they cover complexity, duplication, and premature design, while the CAP theorem belongs to distributed systems, not this LLD principles list.

termDefinitions.meaning: KISS（Keep It Simple, Stupid）：优先选能工作的最简单方案，而不是炫技的复杂设计。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: KISS stands for Keep It Simple, Stupid, meaning you should prefer the simplest design that actually works.

termDefinitions.meaning: DRY（Don't Repeat Yourself）：概念上相同的逻辑只维护一处。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DRY stands for Don't Repeat Yourself, meaning conceptually identical logic should live in one place.

termDefinitions.meaning: YAGNI（You Aren't Gonna Need It）：只实现当前需求真正要求的功能。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: YAGNI stands for You Aren't Gonna Need It, meaning you should only build what current requirements actually need.

termDefinitions.meaning: CAP 定理：分布式系统里一致性、可用性、分区容忍性最多同时满足两项。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The CAP theorem says a distributed system can fully guarantee only two of consistency, availability, and partition tolerance at once.

scenario: 停车场题需求只要求停普通车、查空位，候选人却想引入五层工厂、装饰器和插件系统。
scenario_en: The parking-lot prompt only asks for parking a car and checking free spots, but the candidate wants five layers of factories, decorators, and a plugin system.
q: 面对这种过度设计冲动，哪个原则最该提醒他？
q_en: Which principle should rein in this urge to over-design?
options: Observer
KISS
分布式一致性
读写锁
options_en: the Observer pattern
KISS
distributed consistency
a read-write lock
why: KISS 要求先用能工作的最简单设计，复杂模式只有在简单设计撑不住真实变化时才加。
why_en: KISS says start with the simplest design that works and add complex patterns only once simplicity actually breaks down.
whenOtherWins: 如果 follow-up 明确要求多种可插拔计费或复杂扩展，再引入 Observer 等模式才合理。
tradeoff: 简单可行方案 vs 提前展示模式知识

termDefinitions.meaning: KISS（Keep It Simple, Stupid）：优先选能工作的最简单方案。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: KISS stands for Keep It Simple, Stupid, meaning prefer the simplest design that works.

termDefinitions.meaning: Observer（观察者模式）：让订阅者在被观察对象状态变化时自动收到通知。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Observer pattern lets subscribers get notified automatically when an observed object's state changes.

q: LLD 面试中过度设计最常见的坏处是什么？
q_en: What is the most common downside of overengineering in an LLD interview?
options: 一定能拿到更高分
能自动满足所有未来需求
核心逻辑被模式层级淹没，还更难维护
会减少你解释设计的时间成本
options_en: It always earns a higher score.
It automatically satisfies every future requirement.
It buries the core logic under pattern layers and hurts maintainability.
It reduces the time you spend explaining the design.
why: 过多模式和层级会把简单问题变复杂；面试时间有限，复杂结构还会增加 bug 和沟通成本。
why_en: Too many patterns and layers bury simple logic, and with limited interview time the extra structure adds bugs and communication overhead.

q: DRY 的真正关注点是什么？
q_en: What does DRY actually care about?
options: 任何看起来相似的代码都必须立刻抽象
永远不能写两行相似的代码
所有类必须继承同一个父类
概念上相同的逻辑应该集中维护
options_en: Any code that looks similar must be abstracted immediately.
You must never write two similar-looking lines of code.
Every class must inherit from the same parent class.
Logic that is conceptually the same should be maintained in one place.
why: DRY 的价值是维护一致性：规则变了只改一处；文本相似但业务目的不同的代码不必强行合并。
why_en: DRY is about maintaining consistency so a rule change touches only one place, not about merging code that merely looks similar but serves different purposes.

termDefinitions.meaning: DRY（Don't Repeat Yourself）：概念上相同的逻辑只维护一处。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DRY stands for Don't Repeat Yourself, meaning conceptually identical logic should live in one place.

q: DRY 和 KISS 冲突时，成熟的回答应该是什么？
q_en: When DRY and KISS conflict, what does a mature answer sound like?
options: 承认权衡：先保持简单，等重复稳定出现再抽象
永远立刻抽象
永远允许无限复制
只按代码行数决定要不要抽象
options_en: Acknowledge the tradeoff: stay simple first, then abstract once duplication is stable.
Always abstract immediately.
Always allow unlimited duplication.
Decide purely by counting lines of code.
why: 强行抽象会制造人工耦合；说清楚“现在先简单，重复多处且概念相同时再提取”是更稳的判断。
why_en: Forcing an early abstraction creates artificial coupling, so the safer call is staying simple now and extracting only once the same-concept duplication is stable.
tradeoff: DRY 的集中维护 vs KISS 的当下简单

termDefinitions.meaning: DRY（Don't Repeat Yourself）：概念上相同的逻辑只维护一处。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DRY stands for Don't Repeat Yourself, meaning conceptually identical logic should live in one place.

termDefinitions.meaning: KISS（Keep It Simple, Stupid）：优先选能工作的最简单方案。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: KISS stands for Keep It Simple, Stupid, meaning prefer the simplest design that works.

scenario: 题目没有提电动车、代客泊车或会员折扣，但候选人准备把这些全部实现。
scenario_en: The prompt never mentions EV charging, valet parking, or membership discounts, yet the candidate plans to implement all of them anyway.
q: 哪个原则最直接反对这种做法？
q_en: Which principle most directly argues against this approach?
options: CAS
YAGNI
LSP
Observer
options_en: CAS
YAGNI
LSP
the Observer pattern
why: YAGNI 是“现在不需要就别先建”；设计时可以留边界，但不要实现猜测中的未来功能。
why_en: YAGNI says not to build a feature before it is actually required, even though you can still leave clean seams for future extension.
whenOtherWins: 当面试官提出具体 follow-up（比如真的要支持电动车）时，再实现对应部分。
tradeoff: 当前需求的边界 vs 提前实现猜测中的未来功能

termDefinitions.meaning: YAGNI（You Aren't Gonna Need It）：只实现当前需求真正要求的功能。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: YAGNI stands for You Aren't Gonna Need It, meaning only build what current requirements actually need.

termDefinitions.meaning: CAS（Compare-And-Swap）：一种无锁并发原语，先比较内存值再原子替换。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CAS stands for Compare-And-Swap, a lock-free concurrency primitive that atomically swaps a value only if it still matches an expected value.

termDefinitions.meaning: LSP（Liskov Substitution Principle）：子类必须能替换父类而不破坏承诺。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LSP stands for Liskov Substitution Principle, meaning subtypes must be usable wherever the base type is expected.

termDefinitions.meaning: Observer（观察者模式）：让订阅者在对象状态变化时自动收到通知。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Observer pattern lets subscribers get notified automatically when an observed object's state changes.

q: “设计时考虑扩展”和“现在就实现未来功能”有什么区别？
q_en: What's the difference between designing with extension in mind and building future features now?
options: 两者含义完全相同，没有区别
前者禁止定义任何抽象接口
前者边界清晰，后者塞入非必要复杂度
后者实现总是比前者更简单
options_en: They mean exactly the same thing.
The former forbids defining any abstract interface.
The former keeps boundaries clean; the latter drags unnecessary complexity into the core design.
The latter is always simpler to implement.
why: 好设计可以为变化留清楚的接缝，但代码只实现当前需求，这样既不锁死未来，也不背负死功能。
why_en: A good design leaves clean seams for future change while the code itself implements only what is required today, avoiding both lock-in and dead features.
tradeoff: 为扩展留接缝 vs 现在就实现未要求的功能

scenario: TicTacToe.play() 方法同时打印棋盘、读用户输入、更新棋盘状态、判断胜负。
scenario_en: A single TicTacToe.play() method prints the board, reads user input, updates board state, and checks for a winner all at once.
q: 这违反了什么原则？
q_en: Which principle does this violate?
options: CAS 原语
Singleton 模式
CAP 定理
关注点分离
options_en: the CAS primitive
the Singleton pattern
the CAP theorem
separation of concerns
why: 显示、输入和游戏规则是不同的变化原因，混在一个方法里会让测试、换 UI、改规则都变难。
why_en: Display, input, and game rules change for different reasons, so mixing them in one method makes testing, swapping the UI, and changing rules all harder.
whenOtherWins: 极小 demo 可以先写在一起，但面试设计应该展示清晰的职责边界。
tradeoff: 单方法的开发速度 vs 拆类后的可测试性

termDefinitions.meaning: CAS（Compare-And-Swap）：一种无锁并发原语。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CAS stands for Compare-And-Swap, a lock-free concurrency primitive.

termDefinitions.meaning: Singleton（单例模式）：保证一个类全局只有一个实例。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Singleton pattern ensures a class has only one instance globally.

termDefinitions.meaning: CAP 定理：一致性、可用性、分区容忍性最多同时满足两项。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The CAP theorem says a distributed system can fully guarantee only two of consistency, availability, and partition tolerance.

termDefinitions.meaning: Separation of Concerns（关注点分离）：把显示、输入、业务规则等不同变化原因拆到各自的类里。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Separation of Concerns means responsibilities like display, input, and business rules should live in their own classes.

q: 把 Board、Display、InputHandler 拆开有哪些好处？（多选）
q_en: What are the benefits of splitting Board, Display, and InputHandler into separate classes? (multi-select)
options: 让所有类互相知道对方的内部字段
可以单独替换输入方式
可以单独修改显示方式
可以独立测试游戏规则
options_en: It lets every class know the others' internal fields.
You can swap the input method independently.
You can change the display independently.
You can test the game rules independently.
why: 关注点分离让变化局部化；类之间不应通过暴露内部字段来协作。
why_en: Separating concerns localizes change, and classes should not collaborate by exposing their internal fields to each other.
diagram:
flowchart LR
I["InputHandler"] --> G["Game rules"]
G --> B["Board state"]
G --> D["Display/View"]
T["tests"] --> G
D --> U["UI output"]

q: Law of Demeter 主要想避免什么？
q_en: What is the Law of Demeter mainly trying to avoid?
options: 调用方穿透多层对象了解内部结构
所有方法调用
所有构造函数
所有接口
options_en: Callers reaching through multiple layers of objects to learn internal structure.
Every method call.
Every constructor.
Every interface.
why: 像 order.getCustomer().getAddress().getZipCode() 这样的链式访问会让调用方耦合到三个对象的内部结构；更好的做法是在 Order 上提供更高层方法。
why_en: Deep chains like order.getCustomer().getAddress().getZipCode() couple the caller to three objects' internals, so it is better to expose a higher-level method on Order instead.

termDefinitions.meaning: Law of Demeter（最少知识原则）：一个方法只应该和它的直接朋友对象交流，不穿透多层对象访问内部结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Law of Demeter says a method should only talk to its immediate collaborators, not reach through layers of objects to access internal structure.

q: 为什么 builder.setName(...).setAge(...).build() 通常不算 Law of Demeter 问题？
q_en: Why doesn't builder.setName(...).setAge(...).build() usually count as a Law of Demeter violation?
options: 因为链式调用永远安全
都在同一个构建器上连续设置，没有穿透其他对象
因为 Builder 模式不需要封装
因为它只存在于 Python 语言里
options_en: Because chained calls are always safe.
Every call stays on the same builder instance, so it never reaches through other objects' internals.
Because the Builder pattern doesn't need encapsulation.
Because it only exists in the Python language.
why: 问题不是点号数量，而是是否暴露并依赖多个对象的内部层级；流式接口通常在同一个抽象上连续配置。
why_en: The issue is not how many dots you chain, but whether you traverse multiple objects' internals, and a fluent builder keeps every call on the same abstraction.
tradeoff: 同一对象上连续配置 vs 穿透多个不同对象的内部结构

termDefinitions.meaning: Law of Demeter（最少知识原则）：只和直接朋友对象交流，不穿透内部结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Law of Demeter says a method should only talk to its immediate collaborators, not reach through object internals.

termDefinitions.meaning: Builder（构造器模式）：用链式方法逐步设置字段，最后调用 build() 生成对象。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Builder pattern sets fields step by step through chained calls and produces the final object with a build() call.

q: 补全 SOLID 五项：
q_en: Fill in the five SOLID letters:
why: 不必机械背诵，但要知道每项背后的设计判断。面试里更重要的是应用而不是报缩写。
why_en: SOLID stands for Single Responsibility, Open Closed, Liskov Substitution, Interface Segregation, and Dependency Inversion.

termDefinitions.fullName: Single Responsibility, Open/Closed, Liskov Substitution, Interface Segregation, Dependency Inversion
termDefinitions.meaning: SOLID：五项面向对象设计原则的合称，分别对应类职责、扩展方式、子类替换、接口粒度、依赖方向。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SOLID is the acronym for five object-oriented design principles covering class responsibility, extension, substitution, interface size, and dependency direction.

scenario: Report 类同时生成报告内容、格式化 PDF、还要把结果保存到文件。
scenario_en: A single Report class generates the content, formats it as PDF, and also saves the result to a file.
q: 最直接违反了什么原则？
q_en: Which principle does this most directly violate?
options: Actor
Observer
SRP
YAGNI
options_en: the Actor model
the Observer pattern
SRP
YAGNI
why: 内容生成、PDF 格式化、文件存储是三个不同的变化原因；拆成 Report、PDFPrinter、FileStorage 能让每类的变化互不牵连。
why_en: Content generation, PDF formatting, and file storage change for different reasons, so splitting them into Report, PDFPrinter, and FileStorage isolates each change.
whenOtherWins: 如果只是一次性脚本且不会扩展，简单函数也可能够用；面试里的可维护设计通常应该拆职责。
tradeoff: 单类的开发速度 vs 拆分后每个变化互不影响

termDefinitions.meaning: Actor（Actor 模型）：把并发单元建模成互相发消息、各自维护状态的独立实体。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Actor model treats each concurrent unit as an independent entity that keeps its own state and communicates only via messages.

termDefinitions.meaning: Observer（观察者模式）：让订阅者在对象状态变化时自动收到通知。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Observer pattern lets subscribers get notified automatically when an observed object's state changes.

termDefinitions.meaning: SRP（Single Responsibility Principle）：一个类应该只有一个改变的理由。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SRP stands for Single Responsibility Principle, meaning a class should have only one reason to change.

termDefinitions.meaning: YAGNI（You Aren't Gonna Need It）：只实现当前需求真正要求的功能。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: YAGNI stands for You Aren't Gonna Need It, meaning only build what current requirements actually need.

q: 「一个类应该只有一个改变理由」描述的是哪项原则？
q_en: "A class should have only one reason to change" describes which principle?
options: DIP
OCP
LSP
SRP
options_en: DIP
OCP
LSP
SRP
why: SRP 不代表类只能有一个方法，而是它的职责要凝聚，变化原因不能混杂。
why_en: SRP does not mean a class can only have one method — it means its responsibilities stay cohesive and its reasons to change do not mix.

termDefinitions.meaning: DIP（Dependency Inversion Principle）：高层业务应依赖抽象而不是具体实现。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DIP stands for Dependency Inversion Principle, meaning high-level logic should depend on abstractions.

termDefinitions.meaning: OCP（Open/Closed Principle）：对扩展开放、对修改关闭。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: OCP stands for Open/Closed Principle, meaning code should be open for extension but closed for modification.

termDefinitions.meaning: LSP（Liskov Substitution Principle）：子类必须能替换父类而不破坏承诺。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LSP stands for Liskov Substitution Principle, meaning subtypes must be usable wherever the base type is expected.

termDefinitions.meaning: SRP（Single Responsibility Principle）：一个类应该只有一个改变的理由。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SRP stands for Single Responsibility Principle, meaning a class should have only one reason to change.

scenario: PaymentProcessor 用 if/elif 判断 credit、paypal 分支；每加一种支付方式都要改这个方法。
scenario_en: PaymentProcessor branches on payment_type with if/elif for credit and paypal, so every new payment method means editing this same method.
q: 更符合 OCP 的设计是什么？
q_en: Which design better follows OCP here?
options: 定义 PaymentMethod 接口，让 processor 只依赖接口而不是分支
继续在 process() 里累加 if/elif 分支判断
把每种支付方式都写成模块级全局字符串
让上层 UI 组件直接跳过 processor 处理支付
options_en: Define a PaymentMethod interface so the processor depends on the interface, not on branches.
Keep stacking if/elif branches inside process().
Turn every payment type into a module-level global string.
Let the UI layer skip the processor and handle payment itself.
why: OCP 希望新增行为通过新增实现类完成，而不是反复修改已验证过的旧代码；接口把变化点隔离出来。
why_en: OCP wants new behavior added through new implementation classes instead of repeatedly editing already-verified code, and the interface isolates the variation point.
whenOtherWins: 如果只有两种支付方式且以后不会扩展，简单分支可能更符合 KISS。
tradeoff: 扩展新支付方式的安全性 vs 引入接口的抽象成本

termDefinitions.meaning: OCP（Open/Closed Principle）：对扩展开放、对修改关闭。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: OCP stands for Open/Closed Principle, meaning code should be open for extension but closed for modification.

termDefinitions.meaning: KISS（Keep It Simple, Stupid）：优先选能工作的最简单方案。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: KISS stands for Keep It Simple, Stupid, meaning prefer the simplest design that works.

classDiagram

  +process(method,order)
}

  <<interface>>
  +pay(order)
}

class PayPalPayment
class CryptoPayment

PaymentMethod <|.. CreditCardPayment
PaymentMethod <|.. PayPalPayment

q: OCP 的核心取舍是什么？
q_en: What is the core tradeoff of OCP?
options: 只适用于数据库场景
降低修改旧代码的风险，但需要提前认准真实的变化点
禁止创建任何新类
要求所有逻辑写进一个方法里
options_en: It only applies to database scenarios.
It lowers the risk of editing old code, but only pays off once you've spotted a real variation point.
It forbids creating any new classes.
It requires writing all logic into a single method.
why: 接口能让扩展更安全，但抽象本身有成本，只有变化点明确时才值得引入。
why_en: Interfaces make extension safer, but abstraction itself has a cost, so it only pays off once the variation point is real.
tradeoff: 回归风险降低 vs 抽象层的认知与维护成本

termDefinitions.meaning: OCP（Open/Closed Principle）：对扩展开放、对修改关闭。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: OCP stands for Open/Closed Principle, meaning code should be open for extension but closed for modification.

scenario: Bird 基类定义了 fly()，Penguin 继承 Bird，但 fly() 里只能抛异常。
scenario_en: The Bird base class defines fly(), and Penguin extends Bird but its fly() can only raise an exception.
q: 这违反了什么原则？
q_en: Which principle does this violate?
options: DRY
Facade
LSP
YAGNI
options_en: DRY
the Facade pattern
LSP
YAGNI
why: 调用方以为任何 Bird 都能 fly，传入 Penguin 却破坏了这个承诺；基类不该承诺并非所有子类都能兑现的行为。
why_en: Callers assume every Bird can fly, but passing in a Penguin breaks that promise, so the base type should not guarantee behavior not every subtype can honor.
whenOtherWins: 如果基类只承诺 eat()，飞行能力单独放进 FlyingBird，Penguin 实现 Bird 就没问题。
tradeoff: 统一的 Bird 接口 vs 按能力拆分的子接口

termDefinitions.meaning: DRY（Don't Repeat Yourself）：概念上相同的逻辑只维护一处。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DRY stands for Don't Repeat Yourself, meaning conceptually identical logic should live in one place.

termDefinitions.meaning: Facade（外观模式）：给一组复杂子系统提供一个更简单的统一接口。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Facade pattern provides one simplified interface in front of a set of complex subsystems.

termDefinitions.meaning: LSP（Liskov Substitution Principle）：子类必须能替换父类而不破坏承诺。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LSP stands for Liskov Substitution Principle, meaning subtypes must be usable wherever the base type is expected.

termDefinitions.meaning: YAGNI（You Aren't Gonna Need It）：只实现当前需求真正要求的功能。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: YAGNI stands for You Aren't Gonna Need It, meaning only build what current requirements actually need.

q: LSP 在类层次设计中提醒你注意什么？
q_en: What does LSP remind you to watch for when designing a class hierarchy?
options: 父类必须知道所有子类
子类必须覆写所有方法
继承永远优于组合
子类不能破坏父类或接口对调用方的承诺
options_en: The base class must know about every subclass.
Subclasses must override every method.
Inheritance is always better than composition.
Subtypes must not break the promises the base type or interface makes to callers.
why: 如果调用方需要 instanceof 特判，或子类方法抛“我不支持”，这条继承链通常已经出问题。
why_en: If callers need instanceof checks or a subclass throws an unsupported-method exception, the hierarchy is usually already broken.

termDefinitions.meaning: LSP（Liskov Substitution Principle）：子类必须能替换父类而不破坏承诺。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LSP stands for Liskov Substitution Principle, meaning subtypes must be usable wherever the base type is expected.

scenario: Robot 被迫实现 eat() 和 sleep()，虽然机器人其实只会 work()。
scenario_en: Robot is forced to implement eat() and sleep(), even though a robot really only does work().
q: 更符合 ISP 的做法是什么？
q_en: Which approach better follows ISP here?
options: 拆成 Workable/Feedable/Restable 等小接口
让 Robot 的 eat() 空着不实现
在 eat() 里直接抛异常
把所有方法塞进一个巨大 Worker 接口
options_en: Split it into small interfaces like Workable, Feedable, Restable.
Leave Robot's eat() as an empty implementation.
Make eat() raise an exception directly.
Cram every method into one giant Worker interface.
why: ISP 反对胖接口；类只应该依赖和实现自己真正需要的能力。
why_en: ISP argues against fat interfaces — a class should only depend on and implement the capabilities it actually needs.
whenOtherWins: 如果所有实现确实都需要同一组方法，保留一个完整接口也可以。
tradeoff: 接口数量增多 vs 类不必实现无关方法

termDefinitions.meaning: ISP（Interface Segregation Principle）：接口应该小而专注。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ISP stands for Interface Segregation Principle, meaning interfaces should be small and focused.

q: 胖接口通常会带来哪些坏味道？（多选）
q_en: Which code smells does a fat interface usually cause? (multi-select)
options: 空实现
更清晰的职责边界
抛「不支持」异常的方法
类被迫依赖无关能力
options_en: empty implementations
clearer responsibility boundaries
methods that throw an unsupported exception
classes forced to depend on unrelated capabilities
why: 胖接口把无关职责绑在一起；小接口能按能力组合，减少虚假实现。
why_en: A fat interface bundles unrelated responsibilities together, while small interfaces compose by capability and avoid fake implementations.

scenario: NotificationService 的构造函数里直接 new EmailSender，测试会真的发邮件，改 SMS 也要改这个服务。
scenario_en: NotificationService directly news up an EmailSender in its constructor, so tests send real emails and switching to SMS means editing this service.
q: 更符合 DIP 的设计是什么？
q_en: Which design better follows DIP here?
options: 把 EmailSender 做成全局变量
依赖 MessageSender 接口，通过构造函数注入具体实现
在 notify() 里加更多 if 判断渠道
让单元测试直接连接真实邮件服务
options_en: Turn EmailSender into a global variable.
Depend on a MessageSender interface and inject the concrete sender through the constructor.
Add more if-branches inside notify() for each channel.
Let unit tests connect to the real email service directly.
why: DIP 要求高层业务依赖抽象而不是具体实现；构造注入是实现 DIP 的常见技术，也顺带提升了可测试性。
why_en: DIP requires high-level logic to depend on an abstraction rather than a concrete class, and constructor injection is the common technique that also improves testability.
whenOtherWins: 非常简单且不会替换实现的脚本可以直接 new，但面试里的服务设计通常应该暴露依赖边界。
tradeoff: 直接 new 的简单性 vs 依赖抽象带来的可测试性

termDefinitions.meaning: DIP（Dependency Inversion Principle）：高层业务应依赖抽象而不是具体实现。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DIP stands for Dependency Inversion Principle, meaning high-level logic should depend on abstractions rather than concrete implementations.

q: DIP 和 dependency injection 的关系是什么？
q_en: What is the relationship between DIP and dependency injection?
options: 依赖注入是原则，DIP 是 Python 语法
两者完全无关
DIP 是设计原则，依赖注入是实现它的常见技术
DIP 要求所有对象都必须是 Singleton
options_en: Dependency injection is the principle and DIP is Python syntax.
The two are completely unrelated.
DIP is the design principle, and dependency injection is a common technique for implementing it.
DIP requires every object to be a Singleton.
why: DIP 说的是依赖要指向抽象；DI 是通过构造函数、参数或容器把具体实现传进来的技术手段。
why_en: DIP says dependencies should point at abstractions, while DI is the technique of passing concrete implementations in via constructors, parameters, or a container.
tradeoff: DIP 定义“依赖什么” vs DI 提供“怎么传进来”

termDefinitions.meaning: DIP（Dependency Inversion Principle）：高层业务应依赖抽象而不是具体实现。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DIP stands for Dependency Inversion Principle, meaning high-level logic should depend on abstractions rather than concrete implementations.

termDefinitions.meaning: DI（依赖注入）：把对象依赖的具体实现从外部传入，而不是在内部自己创建。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DI stands for Dependency Injection, a technique that passes an object's dependencies in from the outside instead of creating them internally.

termDefinitions.meaning: Singleton（单例模式）：保证一个类全局只有一个实例。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Singleton pattern ensures a class has only one instance globally.

q: 把用 OCP 重构支付处理的步骤排好：
q_en: Put these OCP-driven steps for refactoring payment handling in order:
steps: 新增 CreditCardPayment、PayPalPayment 等实现类
识别变化点是支付方式
让 PaymentProcessor 依赖 PaymentMethod 接口
新增 CryptoPayment 时不改 PaymentProcessor
why: 先找变化点，再抽象接口，最后通过新增实现扩展。这样才是为真实变化服务的 OCP。
why_en: OCP refactoring starts by identifying the payment variation point, introducing an interface, and adding implementations without changing the processor.
tradeoff: 先识别变化点再抽象 vs 直接一次性大重构

termDefinitions.meaning: OCP（Open/Closed Principle）：对扩展开放、对修改关闭。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: OCP stands for Open/Closed Principle, meaning code should be open for extension but closed for modification.

diagram:
flowchart TD
A["identify payment as variation point"] --> B["define PaymentMethod interface"]
B --> C["add concrete implementations"]
C --> D["processor calls abstraction"]
D --> E["new payment type adds class only"]

scenario: 类 A 调用 order.getCustomer().getAddress().getZipCode() 来完成订单规则判断。
scenario_en: Class A calls order.getCustomer().getAddress().getZipCode() just to run an order rule check.
q: 最直接可以怎么改？
q_en: What is the most direct fix here?
options: 把 zipCode 放进全局变量
让 A 直接继承 Address
把 Customer 和 Address 的字段都设为 public
让 Order 提供 getCustomerZipCode() 这样的高层方法
options_en: Put zipCode into a global variable.
Have A inherit directly from Address.
Make every Customer and Address field public.
Have Order expose a higher-level method like getCustomerZipCode().
why: 调用方不该知道对象内部的嵌套结构；让拥有聚合关系的对象提供贴近需求的方法，能直接降低耦合。
why_en: Callers should not need to know an object's internal nesting, so letting the aggregate owner expose a purpose-built method directly reduces coupling.
whenOtherWins: 简单 DTO 序列化场景里，浅层字段访问可能可以接受，但业务规则不应该这样穿透。
tradeoff: Order 承担导航逻辑 vs 调用方自己穿透对象图

termDefinitions.meaning: Law of Demeter（最少知识原则）：只和直接朋友对象交流，不穿透内部结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Law of Demeter says a method should only talk to its immediate collaborators, not reach through object internals.

scenario: 业务逻辑类里直接拼格式化字符串给 UI 展示，同时还在同一个方法里更新核心状态。
scenario_en: A business-logic class formats display strings for the UI directly, inside the very same method that also updates core state.
q: 更好的责任边界是什么？
q_en: What is a better responsibility boundary here?
options: 业务类管规则和状态，展示交给 Display 层
把所有格式化逻辑都塞进数据库层
让 UI 层直接改业务状态字段
把核心状态字段整个删除掉
options_en: The business class owns rules and state; the display layer owns formatting.
Push all formatting logic down into the database layer.
Let the UI layer edit business state fields directly.
Delete the core state fields entirely.
why: 展示变化和业务规则变化是不同的原因；拆开后 UI 改版不需要碰业务状态机。
why_en: Presentation changes and business-rule changes happen for different reasons, so separating them means a UI redesign never touches the business state machine.
whenOtherWins: 一次性命令行 demo 可以合并输出逻辑，但面试设计应该展示可维护的边界。
tradeoff: 合并输出的开发速度 vs 拆分后 UI 改版不影响业务状态

q: 在现代代码库里，应该如何看待 SOLID 原则的分量？
q_en: How much weight should SOLID carry in a modern codebase?
options: 已经完全没有意义
仍然有用，但不该为套 SOLID 破坏 KISS
必须完整套用每一条，不能省略
只适用于系统设计面试，不适用于 LLD
options_en: It is completely meaningless now.
Still useful, but don't break KISS just to force-fit SOLID.
You must apply every single letter, no exceptions.
It only applies to system-design interviews, not LLD.
why: SOLID 来自继承和接口较重的时代；现在仍可用，但应该服务于问题，而不是制造不必要的复杂度。
why_en: SOLID comes from an era of heavy inheritance and interfaces, and it is still useful, but it should serve the problem rather than create unnecessary complexity.
tradeoff: SOLID 的结构清晰度 vs KISS 的当下简单

termDefinitions.fullName: Single Responsibility, Open/Closed, Liskov Substitution, Interface Segregation, Dependency Inversion
termDefinitions.meaning: SOLID：五项面向对象设计原则的合称。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SOLID is the acronym for five object-oriented design principles.

termDefinitions.meaning: KISS（Keep It Simple, Stupid）：优先选能工作的最简单方案。

termDefinitions.meaning: LLD（Low-Level Design）：聚焦类、接口、对象交互的详细设计面试环节。

q: 哪些「场景 → 原则」映射是合理的？（多选）
q_en: Which "scenario → principle" mappings are reasonable? (multi-select)
options: 类混合多个变化原因 → SRP
新增类型总要改旧方法 → OCP
对象有很多可选参数 → Law of Demeter
子类不能支持父类方法 → LSP
options_en: A class mixes multiple reasons to change → SRP
Adding a new type always forces editing old methods → OCP
An object has many optional parameters → Law of Demeter
A subclass can't support a parent method → LSP
why: 很多可选参数更可能指向 Builder 或构造 API 的设计问题，不是 Law of Demeter。
why_en: Many optional parameters more likely point to a Builder or constructor-API design issue, not a Law of Demeter violation.
tradeoff: 对症选出正确的原则名称 vs 套用相近但不对的原则

termDefinitions.meaning: SRP（Single Responsibility Principle）：一个类应该只有一个改变的理由。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SRP stands for Single Responsibility Principle, meaning a class should have only one reason to change.

termDefinitions.meaning: OCP（Open/Closed Principle）：对扩展开放、对修改关闭。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: OCP stands for Open/Closed Principle, meaning code should be open for extension but closed for modification.

termDefinitions.meaning: Law of Demeter（最少知识原则）：只和直接朋友对象交流，不穿透内部结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Law of Demeter says a method should only talk to its immediate collaborators, not reach through object internals.

termDefinitions.meaning: LSP（Liskov Substitution Principle）：子类必须能替换父类而不破坏承诺。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LSP stands for Liskov Substitution Principle, meaning subtypes must be usable wherever the base type is expected.

scenario: 两个类都有相似的字符串格式化代码：一个是用户收据展示，一个是审计日志，两者的变化规则并不同。
scenario_en: Two classes have similar string-formatting code: one renders a user-facing receipt, the other writes an audit log, and their change rules differ.
q: 是否一定要马上抽成共享方法？
q_en: Do they have to be extracted into a shared method right away?
options: 必须放进父类
必须用 Singleton 统一管理
不一定；文本相似不等于概念相同，强抽可能耦合出错
一定要，因为 DRY 禁止任何相似代码
options_en: It must go into a parent class.
It must be centralized through a Singleton.
Not necessarily — similar text isn't the same concept, and forcing an abstraction can create the wrong coupling.
Yes always, because DRY forbids any similar-looking code.
why: DRY 看的是知识重复，不只是文本重复；不同业务目的的相似代码可以先分开，避免未来互相牵连。
why_en: DRY is about duplicated knowledge, not just duplicated text, so similar code serving different business purposes can stay separate to avoid entangling unrelated changes later.
whenOtherWins: 如果两处确实共享同一格式规范，并且会一起变化，抽出共同的 formatter 更合理。
tradeoff: 现在保持独立 vs 提前抽象共享逻辑

termDefinitions.meaning: Singleton（单例模式）：保证一个类全局只有一个实例。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Singleton pattern ensures a class has only one instance globally.

termDefinitions.meaning: DRY（Don't Repeat Yourself）：概念上相同的逻辑只维护一处。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DRY stands for Don't Repeat Yourself, meaning conceptually identical logic should live in one place.

q: 把应用设计原则的健康顺序排好：
q_en: Put the healthy order of applying design principles in sequence:
steps: 选择最小能解决当前问题的结构
从需求和变化点识别真实压力
如果出现重复、耦合或变化困难，再引入抽象或拆分
用原则名称解释取舍但不让名称驱动设计
why: 原则是判断工具，不是预制答案。先看问题，再决定简单结构是否已经不够。
why_en: Healthy principle use starts from real requirements and variation points, then adds only the abstraction needed.
tradeoff: 先看真实需求再决定结构 vs 先套用原则名称再找问题
diagram:
flowchart TD
A["read real requirement"] --> B["choose minimal structure"]
B --> C{"repetition, coupling, or change pain?"}
C -- no --> D["keep design simple"]
C -- yes --> E["introduce focused abstraction"]
E --> F["explain tradeoff with principle name"]

q: 补全通用原则速记：
q_en: Fill in the general-principles cheat sheet:
text: {{KISS}}：先简单；{{DRY}}：减少概念重复；{{YAGNI}}：不要实现未要求的未来。
why: 这三条能覆盖大部分 LLD 过度设计和维护性讨论。
why_en: KISS means start simple, DRY means avoid duplicated knowledge, and YAGNI means do not build speculative futures.

why: 这不是背诵终点，而是面试中解释设计取舍的语言。
why_en: SRP focuses responsibilities, OCP extends behavior safely, LSP preserves contracts, ISP keeps interfaces small, and DIP depends on abstractions.

scenario: OrderService 的方法里直接创建 StripeAPI 实例，导致单元测试必须连上真实的支付服务。
scenario_en: OrderService methods create a StripeAPI instance directly, so unit tests end up hitting the real payment service.
q: 哪项原则和技术最能改善这里的测试性？
q_en: Which principle and technique would most improve testability here?
options: 把所有字段都设成 public 属性
让 StripeAPI 反过来继承 OrderService
直接把相关单元测试删掉
用 DIP 依赖注入 PaymentGateway 接口
options_en: Make every field public.
Have StripeAPI inherit from OrderService instead.
Just delete the relevant unit tests.
Apply DIP and inject a PaymentGateway interface.
why: 依赖抽象之后，测试可以注入 fake 或 mock；业务逻辑不再绑死某个具体的外部服务。
why_en: Once the dependency points at an abstraction, tests can inject a fake or mock and the business logic is no longer tied to one concrete external service.
whenOtherWins: 如果只是一次性脚本，直接调用具体 API 也可能够用；面试里的服务设计通常应优先保留可测边界。
tradeoff: 直接依赖具体 API 的简单性 vs 依赖抽象带来的可测试性

termDefinitions.meaning: DIP（Dependency Inversion Principle）：高层业务应依赖抽象而不是具体实现。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DIP stands for Dependency Inversion Principle, meaning high-level logic should depend on abstractions rather than concrete implementations.

q: 每加一种支付方式都要改 PaymentProcessor，最大的风险是什么？
q_en: What is the biggest risk of editing PaymentProcessor every time a payment method is added?
options: 反复改核心逻辑，增加回归 bug 风险
新增的实现类数量变得太少
接口的数量会变得太多太杂
自动化测试变得完全不需要
options_en: Repeatedly editing core logic raises regression-bug risk.
You end up creating too few new implementation classes.
You end up with too many, too scattered interfaces.
Automated testing becomes completely unnecessary.
why: OCP 想避免的正是稳定代码被反复打开修改；把变化放进新的实现类能缩小回归范围。
why_en: OCP exists precisely to avoid reopening stable code again and again, and pushing change into new implementation classes shrinks the regression surface.

termDefinitions.meaning: OCP（Open/Closed Principle）：对扩展开放、对修改关闭。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: OCP stands for Open/Closed Principle, meaning code should be open for extension but closed for modification.

scenario: CoffeeMachine 类同时管理库存、收款、冲泡配方和屏幕渲染，后续每个新需求都要改它。
scenario_en: CoffeeMachine manages inventory, payment, brew recipes, and screen rendering all at once, so every new requirement means editing it.
q: 你会如何解释重构方向？
q_en: How would you explain the refactoring direction here?
options: 把所有方法都统一改成 static 方法
按变化原因拆成四个协作类分开管理
只在原有方法里继续叠加 if 分支判断
只把类的名字换一个就足够
options_en: Turn every method into a static method.
Split into four collaborating classes by reason to change.
Keep stacking if-branches inside the original method.
Just rename the class and call it done.
why: SRP 不是为了类的数量多，而是让库存、支付、配方、显示的变化互不牵连。
why_en: SRP isn't about having more classes — it's about keeping inventory, payment, recipe, and display changes from tangling with each other.
whenOtherWins: 如果题目只要求最小冲泡流程、不涉及支付和显示，先留一个简单 orchestrator 也可以。
tradeoff: 单类快速起步 vs 拆分后每个变化互不影响
diagram:
flowchart LR
CM["CoffeeMachine orchestrator"] --> I["Inventory"]
CM --> P["Payment"]
CM --> R["Recipe/Brewer"]
CM --> D["Display"]
I --> IR["stock changes"]
P --> PR["payment changes"]
R --> RR["brew rules"]
D --> DR["UI text"]

q: 为什么「接口越多越好」不是正确理解 SOLID？
q_en: Why is "more interfaces is always better" a wrong reading of SOLID?
options: 接口这种语法只能用在 Java 语言里
接口在任何场景下都完全没有成本
接口也有认知成本，只有真实变化点才值得加
接口会自动帮你生成对应的实现代码
options_en: Interfaces only exist as a Java-only syntax feature.
Interfaces never carry any cost in any scenario.
Interfaces have cognitive cost too, so they're worth adding only at a real variation point.
Interfaces automatically generate their implementations for you.
why: 抽象能隔离变化，但也会增加间接层；面试里要展示你知道何时加、何时不加。
why_en: Abstraction isolates change but also adds a layer of indirection, so the interview signal is knowing when to add it and when not to.
tradeoff: 接口带来的扩展安全 vs 额外的间接层认知成本

q_en: Which statements about using these design principles in an interview are reasonable? (multi-select)
options: 不需要不断点名原则
用原则指导决策并解释取舍
原则是思考工具，不是打勾清单
必须在每句话里都提一次 SOLID
options_en: You don't need to keep naming principles out loud.
Use principles to guide decisions and explain tradeoffs.
Principles are thinking tools, not a checklist to tick off.
You must mention SOLID in every single sentence.
why: 好的设计会自然体现原则；刻意报术语不如清楚说明为什么这样拆类或抽象。
why_en: Good design shows the principles naturally, so explaining why you split a class or added an abstraction beats reciting the term names.

termDefinitions.meaning: SOLID：五项面向对象设计原则的合称。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SOLID is the acronym for five object-oriented design principles.

scenario: 面试官问：“为什么不现在就抽象出一个 Validator 服务？”
scenario_en: The interviewer asks: "Why not abstract out a Validator service right now?"
q: 哪个回答最成熟？
q_en: Which answer sounds the most mature?
options: 因为 DRY 原则从来都不重要
我会立刻抽象出所有校验逻辑
Validator 必须做成 Singleton 模式
现在只有 User 一处用，先放 User 里；多处重复再提取
options_en: Because the DRY principle never matters.
I would abstract all validation logic immediately.
Validator must be built as a Singleton.
Only User uses this today, so keep it there for now and extract once the rule repeats in multiple places.
why: 这个回答同时体现了 KISS、DRY 和 YAGNI 的平衡；没有拒绝抽象，只是把它推迟到有证据时再做。
why_en: This answer balances KISS, DRY, and YAGNI at once — it doesn't reject abstraction, it just defers it until there's real evidence for it.
whenOtherWins: 如果需求已经写明多个实体共享同一验证规则，提前抽出 Validator 就合理。
tradeoff: 现在保持简单 vs 提前抽象共享校验逻辑

termDefinitions.meaning: DRY（Don't Repeat Yourself）：概念上相同的逻辑只维护一处。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DRY stands for Don't Repeat Yourself, meaning conceptually identical logic should live in one place.

termDefinitions.meaning: Singleton（单例模式）：保证一个类全局只有一个实例。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Singleton pattern ensures a class has only one instance globally.
